(band=bradypneic)
A 19-year-old white female visits her PCP reporting increased hair growth on her face and arms. She
mentions experiencing irregular menstrual cycles, often with gaps exceeding 3 months, over the past
year. She has no significant medical history and is not sexually active. Physical examination reveals a
well-appearing patient with a BMI of 30 kg/m^2. Her vital signs show: temperature 97.6°F (37°C), blood
pressure 117/79 mmHg, heart rate 82/min, and respiratory rate 9/min. After diagnostic confirmation,
what should be the initial therapeutic approach, and which associated conditions should be evaluated?

Answer Choices: (A) Spironolactone, assess for insulin resistance and depression (B) Combined oral
contraceptives, assess for thyroid dysfunction and depression (C) Metformin, assess for insulin
resistance and cardiovascular disease (D) Lifestyle modifications, assess for insulin resistance and
eating disorders (E) Weight loss, assess for insulin resistance and lipid dysfunction (F) Combined oral
contraceptives, assess for infertility and insulin resistance (G) Metformin, assess for infertility and lipid
dysfunction (H) Lifestyle modifications, assess for thyroid dysfunction and depression (I) Combined oral
contraceptives, assess for insulin resistance and lipid dysfunction (J) Weight loss, assess for sleep
apnea and cardiovascular disease
 A. Lifestyle modifications, assess for thyroid dysfunction and depression
B. Combined oral contraceptives, assess for thyroid dysfunction and depression
C. Lifestyle modifications, assess for insulin resistance and eating disorders
D. Combined oral contraceptives, assess for infertility and insulin resistance
E. Spironolactone, assess for insulin resistance and depression
F. Metformin, assess for infertility and lipid dysfunction
G. Weight loss, assess for insulin resistance and lipid dysfunction
H. Weight loss, assess for sleep apnea and cardiovascular disease
I. Combined oral contraceptives, assess for insulin resistance and lipid dysfunction
J. Metformin, assess for insulin resistance and cardiovascular disease
